2. Facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule may briefly be stated as follows:- 

 The plaintiff instituted the above Title Suit No. 171 of 1983 for a declaration that the registered kabala deed dated 20.2.74 is a deed of usufractuary mortgage and that the plaintiff is entitled to get back the land, described in the schedule to the said deed, hereinafter referred to as the suit land, on the averments inter-alia that the plaintiff borrowed Tk. 5991/- from the vendee, the defendant No. 1 and on consideration of the said loan the plaintiff executed a sale deed on 20.2.74 and on the same date the defendant No. 1 also executed and registered an agreement of reconveyance in favour of the plaintiff. But the defendant No. 1 in violation of the terms of the agreement for reconveyance transferred the suit land to defendant Nos. 2 and 3 by registered Kabalas dated 30.6.79 and 19.7.79. It is also stated in the plaint that at the time of execution of the sale deed dated 20.2.74 the market price of the suit land was about Tk. 15,000/-. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 who are the successive purchasers of the suit land, contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending inter-alia that the alleged agreement of reconveyance was not at all an agreement for reconveyance of the suit land it was an 'ekrarnama' imposing restrictions on further alienation. 

 7. Mr. Mihir Kanti Mazumder, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the sale deed and the deed of agreement to reconvey together constitute a complete usufractuary mortgage under the provision of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and on the expiry of 7 years, the plaintiff who is the vendor of the suit land is entitled to the recovery of the suit land. 

 8. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows:- 

 95A. Treatment of certain transaction as usufructuary Mortgage: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of, such holding or portion or share thereof, for a specified period in line of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of Section 95 shall apply to such transfer, whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order 1972 (P.O. No. 88 of 1972). 

 17. Mr. Mazumder secondly submits that if the said two deeds together namely the deed of sale and the deed of ekrarnama cannot held to be an usufructuary mortgage under Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the plaintiff is at least entitled to a decree, declaring that he has a right to repurchase the suit land on payment of exact consideration money so paid to the vendor namely the plaintiff. 

 24. From the record it appears the plaintiff examined himself as P.W. 1 and has categorically stated in his deposition 

 “আমি সাফ বিক্রয় দেই তাহার একরারনামা দেয়। আসলে উহা বন্ধক ছিল। খায়খালাসী বন্ধক। বিবাদী পক্ষ প্রায় ৬(ছয়) বছর ভোগ করে ধান পায়। তাহাতে যে টাকা আনছিলাম তার দেয় বেশী উসুল হইয়াছে।” Lastly he also stated in his deposition “আমি নির্দায় অবস্থায় জায়গা ফেরত চাই।”
